questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirror on the driver's side.
Use both side mirrors.
Only use the side mirror on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors frequently when backing.

questions.question: If driving a new vehicle, you should learn the controls:

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
Only if you feel you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Learn how all the features and controls work in a new vehicle before you drive it.

questions.question: When passengers have carry-on baggage, it is best to:

options.text: Leave it leaning against the rear exit door.
Leave it near the front door.
Store it so people can reach all exits easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Store it so people can reach all exits easily.
questions.explanation: Never leave baggage in the aisle or at doorways. All baggage must be stored so riders can exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason to change gears?

options.text: Engine speed (rpm)
Road speed (mph)
The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: Change gears based on two things: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range. Watch your speedometer and shift up as you reach higher speeds. Do not shift based on other vehicles.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After every trip
After defects have been repaired
After each fueling

questions.correctAnswerText: After defects have been repaired
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only after any noted defects have been repaired or certified as not needing repair.

questions.question: As a truck driver carrying a load, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Inspecting the cargo.
Recognizing poorly balanced weight.
Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments along your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments along your route.
questions.explanation: As a driver, you must inspect your cargo, recognize overloading or poor weight balance, ensure cargo is properly secured and does not block your view, and confirm cargo does not restrict access to emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be checked:

options.text: For leaks.
For the proper amount of brake fluid.
To ensure they are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an open area away from buildings, trees, and other vehicles.
Pull into a service station.
Tell emergency services where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and park in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Even if your driving test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would handle one at a simulated location.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.
Tire pressure is too low.
Tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will lose points if you:

options.text: Pull up once.
Check your positioning.
Cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each mistake counts against your skills test score.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door for a better look.
Use their mirrors.
Flash their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns. This is especially important during difficult maneuvers.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light stays on after you start the engine, it means:

options.text: The ABS is working properly.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS is not engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light turns on when you start the engine, then turns off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Place weight evenly over the axles.
Not worry about how weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance your cargo properly. Too much weight on one axle damages it and makes steering harder. Too little weight causes poor traction and handling problems.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Grip between the tires and road surface
How fast tires spin
The time it takes to use the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip between the tires and road surface
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip your tires have on the road. Good traction is needed for braking and steering.

questions.question: You should use your horn to:

options.text: Show other drivers you are angry.
Alert other drivers to your presence.
Scare other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert other drivers to your presence.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others you are near. Only use it when needed because it can startle other drivers and create danger.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during an inspection:

options.text: The driver can drive but must go slower.
The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
The vehicle is safe to drive because most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring are dangerous. If one-fourth or more leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: To avoid a crash, you should know that:

options.text: Braking is always the best choice.
Swerving can work better than braking.
You should stay 100 yards behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving can work better than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice. You can usually turn to avoid something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage vehicle parts.
Helps warm up vehicle parts.
Improves fuel efficiency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage vehicle parts.
questions.explanation: Speed up slowly and smoothly to avoid jerking. Rough acceleration causes mechanical damage.

questions.question: After passengers board at a stop, a driver should:

options.text: Give passengers time to sit or hold on before driving.
Honk the horn and enter traffic right away.
Drive as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give passengers time to sit or hold on before driving.
questions.explanation: Start and stop smoothly to prevent passenger injury. Wait for passengers to be seated or braced before you begin driving.
